evals.prompt: our POST /orders endpoint is creating duplicate orders when the mobile client retries on a flaky connection. i need this fixed properly, not just slapping a unique index on it and hoping. spring boot + postgres if it matters
evals.expected_output: Treats this as an idempotency design decision rather than a patch: names the options (naturally idempotent, caller-supplied idempotency key with dedup, uniqueness constraint turning a duplicate into a handled failure) and picks one with reasoning. Addresses what the second call returns. Includes a test that actually exercises a repeated call.

evals.prompt: add an endpoint that takes a CSV upload of products and bulk inserts them. if any row is invalid the whole file should be rejected and nothing written
evals.expected_output: Validates fully before any write, so the all-or-nothing requirement is structural rather than dependent on rollback. Bounds the upload size and row count. Returns actionable per-row errors without leaking internals. Covers the 'nothing was written' half of the requirement in a test against a real boundary, not a mock.

evals.prompt: i've got an acceptance criterion that says 'unsupported formats return 415 before any storage write'. write me the test that proves it. junit 5 and we have testcontainers set up
evals.expected_output: Recognises that mocking the storage layer would encode the very assumption under test, so uses a real boundary. Asserts both halves - the 415 and that nothing was written. Names the test as a claim so it is diagnosable from a failure report. States how to run that one test on its own, and confirms it fails against a deliberately broken implementation.
evals.moved_from: testing (iteration 1). Reassigned after the testing skill was narrowed to end-to-end, level strategy and suite health: an integration test for a server endpoint is written by the engineer implementing it, so this case measures backend.
